issues.legal_issue: Lands added to the schedule by an amendment are subject to the agrarian-reform legislation governing the scheduled estates.
material_facts: The landholders claimed rights and sought ryotwari pattas under legislation applicable to minor inams; some proceedings were pending and some pattas had been issued.
A special investigation recommended bringing the relevant inam villages within the legislation governing inam estates.
An amendment added the landholders’ lands to the schedule of estates covered by that legislation, applied it retrospectively, and displaced proceedings under the minor-inam legislation.
issues.conclusion: The lands added to the schedule were liable to be dealt with under the legislation governing inam estates.
issues.legal_principle: The legislation was intended to carry out agrarian reform by acquiring landholders’ rights in the estates it covered and introducing ryotwari settlements. The amendment made the scheduled lands subject to that legislation.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the validity or application of legislation concerning agrarian land reform.
predicates.lands_added_to_agrarian_reform_schedule: The legislature added the relevant lands to the schedule of lands covered by agrarian-reform legislation.
predicates.scheduled_landholders_rights_are_subject: The legislation provides for changing landholders’ rights in the scheduled lands as part of agrarian reform.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges agrarian-reform legislation and the legislature has scheduled lands for reform that affects landholders’ rights, those lands are subject to the reform.

issues.legal_issue: Legislation providing for acquisition of an estate or rights in agricultural land, or their extinguishment or modification, is protected from challenges based on specified fundamental rights, including when the affected interest is a right to obtain a patta.
material_facts: The challenged amendment brought the landholders’ lands within legislation providing for acquisition of landholders’ rights and ryotwari settlement.
The landholders argued that they had a right to obtain pattas and that the lands should be treated as ryotwari lands rather than estates subject to the legislation.
The challenged legislation formed part of agrarian reform, and the constitutional definition of an estate included ryotwari land and agricultural land.
issues.conclusion: The legislation was protected by Article 31A and could not be challenged on the grounds that it violated Articles 14, 19, or 31, including on the basis that the affected interest was a right to obtain a patta.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(1)(a) protects laws providing for acquisition by the State of an estate or rights in it, or for extinguishment or modification of such rights, from challenges under Articles 14, 19, and 31. Article 31A(2), as amended by the Seventeenth Amendment, includes ryotwari land and land held or let for agriculture within the meaning of “estate.” A right to obtain a patta in respect of agricultural land is also a right that may be affected by such a law. The Court followed Khajamian Wakf Estates v. State of Madras and relied on B. Sankara Rao Badami v. State of Mysore.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging agrarian-reform legislation on constitutional grounds.
predicates.affected_land_is_agricultural_or_ryotwar: The affected land is used or held for agriculture, or is held under a ryotwari settlement.
predicates.affected_interest_is_right_to_pattta: The affected interest includes a claimed right to obtain formal recognition of entitlement to the land.
predicates.law_changes_estate_rights_for_agrarian_r: The law provides for State acquisition of an estate or rights in it, or for their extinguishment or modification, as part of agrarian reform.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges agrarian-reform legislation that changes estate rights, the legislation is protected from the specified fundamental-rights challenge if the affected subject is agricultural or ryotwari land or a right to obtain formal recognition of entitlement.

issues.legal_issue: A legislature does not encroach on judicial power merely by legislating that agrarian-reform legislation applies to specified lands, even where an earlier law provided a process for determining the lands’ tenure.
material_facts: An earlier law allowed interested persons to seek determinations about the tenure of non-ryotwari areas before an administrative officer, with review by a tribunal and the High Court.
The later amendment declared that the agrarian-reform legislation applied to the lands it added to a schedule, and gave that application retrospective effect.
The affected lands could fall within the constitutional meaning of an estate, which included ryotwari lands after the constitutional amendment.
issues.conclusion: The amendment’s declaration that the agrarian-reform legislation applied to the scheduled lands did not encroach on the judicial power of courts.
issues.legal_principle: The legislature could amend the governing law to apply agrarian-reform legislation to specified lands, including ryotwari lands within the constitutional meaning of an estate; the existence of an earlier procedure for deciding questions of tenure did not make that legislative action an exercise of judicial power.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging legislation that specifies lands subject to agrarian reform.
predicates.earlier_law_provided_tenure_adjudication: An earlier law allowed an administrative body and reviewing courts to determine the tenure of the relevant lands.
predicates.legislature_later_specified_lands_for_ag: The legislature later enacted that agrarian-reform legislation applies to specified lands.
predicates.specified_lands_can_fall_within_constitu: The specified lands can fall within the constitutional category of estates subject to agrarian-reform legislation.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a later legislative specification of lands for agrarian reform, the specification is not judicial encroachment if an earlier tenure-adjudication process existed and the lands can fall within the constitutional category of estates.
